extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, attorneys, and counsel dealing with USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) actions or seeking reconsideration/reinstatement
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards applied by the USPTO OED and Director when deciding a Request for Reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. §11.2(d) regarding removal from the register of practitioners, interpretation of practitioner correspondence, and related reinstatement/records procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting practitioner correspondence as a request for removal
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter stating intention to cease practice before the USPTO (for example: 'I am, therefore, ceasing the practice before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office until the Order becomes final or is dissolved or amended...') may be treated by OED as a request to have the practitioner's name removed from the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED's treatment of such language as a removal request is consistent with the plain wording of the practitioner's letter; similar explicit language indicating cessation of practice will be treated as a removal request.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED 30-day response requirement to contest removal
rubrics_metrics.description: OED's letter instructed the practitioner to 'inform us in writing within thirty (30) days from the date of this letter that it is not your intent to have your name removed from the register.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely written notice within 30 days is required to rebut OED's presumption of intent to be removed; failure to provide such notice will result in OED treating the original statement as a valid removal request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond constitutes implicit concurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: If the practitioner does not respond to the OED letter within the prescribed time, that inaction is construed as concurrence in removal from the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision treats non-response as assent; conduct (inaction) is used as evidentiary support for the removal being effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recharacterization of prior communications limited by wording and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner's later attempt to recharacterize earlier correspondence (e.g., claim it was only a name-change notification rather than a request for removal) is disallowed when inconsistent with the original wording and the practitioner's conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent reinterpretations will not override contemporaneous textual evidence and behavior; courts/agency will rely on original text and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED may hold investigations or change-of-status actions in abeyance when state orders/complaints are received
rubrics_metrics.description: OED's March 1996 letter: 'It is our intent to hold in abeyance any investigation with respect to . . . complaint, as well any change of status action based upon the Maryland Court Order, unless you inform us in writing within thirty (30) days...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt of a state court order and complaint can lead OED to pause investigation or status changes, but the practitioner must timely advise if it is not their intent to be removed to avoid change of status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement is subject to regulatory requirements (37 C.F.R. §10.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a practitioner's name is removed from the register, 'you may be reinstated subject to 37 CFR §10.7 ... satisfying the requirements for registration set forth' in the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal is not necessarily permanent, but reinstatement requires meeting the formal regulatory requirements (including, as cited, 37 C.F.R. §10.7) and any other registration prerequisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. §11.2(d) is limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations or issues outside the narrow scope of a Request for Reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. §11.2(d) will not be addressed by the deciding official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only matters properly before the agency under the cited reconsideration provision are considered; other complaints or factual assertions may be referred elsewhere or rejected as outside the purview of the reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records requests must follow FOIA procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for agency records should be made under the Freedom of Information Act: 5 U.S.C. §552; 37 C.F.R. §§102.1-102.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties seeking documents referenced in OED decisions must file FOIA requests per the cited statutes/regulations rather than requesting them via reconsideration pleadings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency decisions under §11.2(d) can be final agency action
rubrics_metrics.description: This decision is characterized as a 'final agency action' under 37 C.F.R. §11.2(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for reconsideration decided under the regulation may result in final administrative decisions, with attendant legal consequences and limited further administrative review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name change does not invalidate removal from the register
rubrics_metrics.description: An assertion that removal was ineffective because the practitioner had changed his name is incorrect; a name change does not negate the validity of removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office treats status-change communications and removal as effective regardless of a practitioner's name-change history; name-change arguments will not automatically nullify removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical evidentiary weight of conduct in determining intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the wording of correspondence and the practitioner's subsequent conduct (e.g., failing to respond, later applying for reinstatement) are relied upon to determine the practitioner's intent regarding removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators will consider documentary language together with later actions (or inaction) when inferring intent; consistent post-hoc explanations inconsistent with earlier conduct are given little weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral of requests beyond reconsideration to OED Director
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for relief other than reconsideration or stay of the Final Decision are referred to the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petitioner seeks forms of relief outside the narrow reconsideration remedy, those claims are not decided under §11.2(d) but forwarded to the OED Director for appropriate action.
